scope: Held-out full-frame evaluation of the conservative rank-16 H3 topology LoRA after epoch 0
summary: The conservative r2 epoch-0 checkpoint generated a complete held-out video but did not repair the robot topology and materially changed the matched motion profile, so the strict RSI contract rejected it.
evidence: The candidate contains 124/124 frames at 832x480 and 24 FPS with SHA-256 3e6b14f29211418214782fd77682f6250448777ed409a38360a7364f6dc3feb7.
Digest-bound semantic review covers every frame: 24 pass and 100 fail, exactly the same 0.193548 topology fraction as the frozen baseline.
Failures begin at frame 24: left shoulder attachment and proportions fail on 100 frames, and the head-to-torso chain fails on 82 frames.
Frozen DINOv2 mean identity changes 0.907582 to 0.907675 and worst-frame identity 0.883382 to 0.886156, but neither can substitute for topology evidence.
Matched motion-profile adherence is 0.941179, below the 0.99 non-regression floor; scene and temporal non-regression gates pass.

The separate flower-action proxy changes motion 0.565746 to 0.564189 and EPL minimum 0.511592 to 0.509141, both within its 0.01 tolerance, demonstrating why both a strict profile gate and task proxy are retained.
The annotated hard-reject demo has SHA-256 7d3bce7bdbdc8a5fa6dd2a76b7fc417c16ae5ad6d13dffef86c52c98fc9722da.
lessons: Longer low-learning-rate replay did not yet alter the visible shoulder failure at epoch 0.
Appearance similarity can improve slightly while action-profile consistency and anatomical topology remain unacceptable.
Every-frame semantic gates must dominate the selection objective; average appearance or task proxies alone would produce a false promotion.
limitations: This is an intermediate epoch-0 checkpoint, not the completed two-epoch r2 round.
The evidence covers one held-out real-scene inspect-flower clip and visible 2-D structure, not universal or physical robot correctness.
The rejected candidate is not a release demo.
next_actions: Let the already-running epoch-1 training finish and repeat the identical held-out generation, full-frame topology review, and non-regression assessment.
If the final r2 checkpoint still shows no topology gain, do not promote it; route to a revised data/architecture candidate instead of weakening the gates.
